title: How US midterm results could affect supply chains
gist: Benchmark expects the Democrats' landslide win in the US midterms to bring closer congressional scrutiny of federal critical minerals deals and slower deal flow. Bipartisan support for cutting reliance on China, especially for defence minerals, should keep government backing for US and allied projects in place. The article is paywalled after the opening quote.

themes.theme: Midterms and US critical minerals deal scrutiny

insights.claim: Benchmark expects the Democrats' landslide victory in the 2026 US midterm elections to mean closer congressional review of the federal government's critical minerals deals.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Government-backed critical minerals deals and their equity stakes face more political and oversight risk.
insights.quote: Federal critical minerals deals are likely to face greater scrutiny following the US midterms
insights.locator: Adam Webb, Benchmark’s head of battery

insights.claim: Benchmark's head of battery raw materials Adam Webb says bipartisan support remains for reducing US reliance on China for critical raw materials, particularly those used in defence applications.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The policy floor under US critical minerals projects is bipartisan, so the change in Congress is unlikely to reverse support.
insights.quote: there remains bipartisan support for reducing reliance on China for these key raw materials, particularly those used in defence applications
insights.locator: Adam Webb, Benchmark’s head of battery

insights.claim: Benchmark expects government backing for critical minerals projects in the US and allied jurisdictions to continue after the midterms, but with a slowdown in deal flow.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Projects waiting on federal deals could see longer timelines, even though backing is still expected.
insights.quote: We therefore expect continued government backing for projects in the US and allied jurisdictions, albeit with a slowdown in deal flow.
insights.locator: Adam Webb, Benchmark’s head of battery
